prompt: Design a workspace settings screen where owners can rename the workspace, transfer ownership, and permanently delete it.
setup: No existing screen is provided. Assume a typical authenticated web application.
must_demonstrate: Identify permanent deletion or ownership transfer as high-consequence actions.
Produce a structural wireframe before polished implementation.
Cover loading, empty, partial, error, success, and offline applicability.
Separate primary settings from destructive actions.
Define confirmation, recovery, or proportional protection.
Produce implementation-ready acceptance criteria before coding.
must_not: Jump directly into React/CSS implementation before the design gate.
Treat Delete Workspace as a normal primary action.
rationale: Exercises intent discovery, risk hierarchy, state completeness, and destructive-action safety.

prompt: Redesign the analytics overview so operators can identify failed jobs faster. The repository already contains DESIGN.md and a component library.
setup: DESIGN.md and reusable components already exist.
must_demonstrate: Inspect or reference the existing design system before proposing new visual values.
Prioritize failed-job detection and operational scanability.
Produce a wireframe and spec before implementation.
Use or deliberately extend existing tokens/components rather than silently forking them.
must_not: Replace the existing design language simply to make the screen look newer.
Default to decorative cards or gradients without a task reason.
rationale: Ensures ux-design respects an existing system and operational density.

prompt: Audit this single screenshot of a checkout form.
setup: Only one static screenshot is available. No runtime, mobile viewport, or keyboard behavior is observable.
must_demonstrate: Separate directly observed issues from inferred or unverified behavior.
Prioritize findings by severity and user impact.
Give a concrete change and verification method for each finding.
Call out runtime, responsive, or keyboard behavior as unverified where appropriate.
must_not: Claim the interface is fully accessible from a screenshot alone.
Assign an arbitrary numerical UX score.
Modify code without a request to fix findings.
rationale: Tests evidence discipline and audit uncertainty.

prompt: Audit the upload-and-processing screen for a transcription product.
setup: The screen supports file selection, upload progress, server processing, failure, retry, cancellation, and completed output.
must_demonstrate: Inspect async state completeness and distinguish upload from processing.
Check queued/running/failed/cancelled/completed feedback.
Evaluate recovery and retry behavior.
Rank missing or ambiguous states above cosmetic polish when they threaten task completion.
must_not: Reduce the audit to visual styling.
Treat a transient toast as sufficient persistent status for long-running work.
rationale: Exercises state completeness and feedback in an asynchronous workflow.

prompt: Review the current diff before merge.
setup: The diff changes a table row action and loading treatment. An unrelated legacy settings page also has known usability issues.
must_demonstrate: Inspect the current diff as the primary scope.
Report UX regressions introduced by the changed table/loading behavior.
Distinguish pre-existing legacy problems from merge-relevant regressions.
Provide patch direction and verification.
must_not: Turn the review into a whole-product audit.
Report unrelated legacy issues as blockers for this merge.

prompt: Review the current diff before merge.
setup: The diff replaces a labeled destructive button with an unlabeled trash icon and changes success copy from 'Draft saved' to 'Done'.
must_demonstrate: Identify loss of affordance and accessible naming risk.
Identify the weaker success/status copy where meaning is lost.
Tie findings to changed files/surfaces and user impact.
Keep severity proportional to actual consequence.
rationale: Exercises affordance and copy review on a small diff.

prompt: Restyle the dashboard to feel more editorial and less generic.
setup: The dashboard behavior, information architecture, and copy are already approved. DESIGN.md exists.
must_demonstrate: Diagnose type, color, space, and finish.
Apply DESIGN.md and explain before/after changes.
Preserve application logic, data flow, information meaning, and copy meaning.
Re-check focus, contrast, status cues, targets, and reduced motion.
must_not: Rewrite approved copy for stylistic reasons.
Re-architect components solely for visual preference.

setup: During inspection, the agent notices that two destructive actions are mixed into the main save flow and require an information-architecture change.
must_demonstrate: Perform only safe visual-system changes that fit the existing structure.
Report the structural UX issue separately as outside restyle scope.
Route structural redesign work to ux-design.
Return a before/after for the visual changes actually made.
must_not: Silently change the workflow or information architecture under a restyle request.
rationale: Ensures restyle reports structural problems without expanding its own scope.
